title: Principal Architect - Payments & Ledger
description:
YouTrip is the leading and fastest\-growing multi\-currency payment platform in Asia Pacific. In 2018, we pioneered the region's first multi\-currency digital wallet. Now, YouTrip is the \#1 multi\-currency digital wallet trusted by millions across the region, processing over US$15 billion in total payment value annually.


Our consumer and business propositions – YouTrip and YouBiz – empower individuals and businesses with inclusive, accessible, and affordable financial solutions. YouTrip has raised over US$110 million to date, including its recent Series B round led by global venture capital firm Lightspeed Venture Partners—underscoring strong investor confidence in its mission to transform digital financial services across the Asia Pacific.


Recognised as World Economic Forum’s Global Innovator 2025, CNBC’s World’s Top Fintech Companies (2025, 2024\), and LinkedIn’s Top Startup (2024, 2023\), YouTrip is dedicated to creating the next generation of digital finance services for consumers and businesses.


Valuing an entrepreneurial culture of diversity and inclusion, we are seeking driven individuals to join our fast\-growing regional team as we push the boundaries of innovative fintech solutions.


Job Description: Principal Architect, Payments \& Ledger

  

You'll own the architectural direction for money movement end to end: multi\-currency wallets and balances, the core ledger, card issuing and authorisation, in\-app FX, overseas transfers and payouts, treasury and pre\-funding, settlement and reconciliation, and the shared platform services underneath them. Your remit covers both YouTrip (consumer) and YouBiz (business), across every market we operate in.


Responsibilities:

* The Ledger \- Double\-entry design, chart of accounts, sub\-ledger boundaries, immutability and correction rules, multi\-currency representation, precision and rounding policy, and how balances are derived or stored. You'll define how we handle authorisation holds, reversals, partial and incremental captures, refunds, FX revaluation and unreconciled positions, and you'll be able to explain and defend those choices to Finance, auditors and regulators.
* Money movement correctness \- Idempotency, exactly\-once outcomes on top of at\-least\-once messaging, clear state machines for every transaction type, and well\-defined failure, retry, timeout and compensation paths. For every integration, the question "what happens if the partner succeeds and we fail?" should have a written answer that you own.
* Card issuing \- Architecture for authorisation, clearing and settlement as a Mastercard Principal Member, including real\-time authorisation on the scheme's critical path, stand\-in processing, authorisation expiry, disputes and chargebacks, tokenisation for Apple Pay and Google Pay, virtual and physical card lifecycle, and the strict latency and availability targets that come with it.
* FX and multi\-currency wallets \- Rate sourcing, quoting and rate locking, spread and exposure management, in\-app currency exchange across our wallet currencies, and pre\-funding and liquidity models that keep customers' balances safe and available.
* Cross\-border transfers \- Corridor architecture, payout rail integrations (local real\-time rails, bank transfers, SWIFT and partner networks), pre\-funding and nostro design, and sanctions and AML screening built in as a core design constraint, not an afterthought.
* Reconciliation and settlement \- We treat reconciliation as an architecture problem, not an operations task. You'll design systems where breaks are rare, spotted within minutes, and traceable to a clear cause, across multiple time zones, currencies and partners.
* Non\-functional requirements \- Latency, throughput, availability and cost as design targets with numbers attached. Clear, written decisions on where eventual consistency is acceptable and where it isn't. Recovery, replay and backfill as built\-in capabilities.
* Standards and technical judgement \- Engineering and coding standards, architecture reviews for significant changes, and architecture documentation that engineers actually build from. You'll write decision records that capture the reasoning and the options rejected, and keep them current.
* Partners and vendors \- Technical evaluation and ongoing oversight of card processors, scheme connectivity, banking and settlement partners, FX liquidity providers, payout partners, KYC and screening vendors, and core infrastructure. You'll know their systems' failure modes as well as their own architects do.
* Growing technical leaders \- You'll mentor tech leads and senior engineers from day one and lead mostly through influence. As the function matures, you'll build and lead a small architecture group.

  

**Requirements**  

* Deep payments and ledger experience (essential) \- You've designed or substantially rebuilt a production financial ledger. You can speak from real experience about journal design, posting models, balance consistency and correction strategies, including what happens when they go wrong.
* Card issuing expertise \- Hands\-on experience with card scheme integrations (ideally Mastercard), issuer processing, authorisation flows, clearing files, and disputes.
* A builder, not just an advisor \- You've written production code at scale, and your work sits behind systems that handled real traffic and real money. Your authority comes from having shipped.
* Range from system to field level \- You're equally comfortable designing distributed settlement flows and deciding the type and precision of a single amount field, often in the same week.
* Regulated\-environment fluency \- Experience with safeguarding and customer fund segregation, payment and e\-money licensing, data residency, auditability and technology risk requirements, ideally including MAS and other Asia Pacific regulators. You design ahead of regulatory and scheme changes instead of reacting to them.
* Multi\-market experience \- You've built systems that operate across several countries, currencies and regulators at once.
* Strong writing \- Clear, structured, opinionated documents that remain useful long after the meeting ends. Documentation is part of the work, not a follow\-up task.
* Opinions you can defend \- Clear positions on design patterns, standards and trade\-offs, explained just as well to a new graduate as to the board.
* Credibility with partners \- You can tell when a vendor's recommendation serves them more than us, and you can make that case with evidence.
* Experience with Golang, event\-driven architectures and cloud\-native infrastructure is a plus.


What This Role Is Not


This isn't a diagramming role, and it isn't a review gate that approves other people's work without contributing to it. It's also not an engineering management role with large headcount or delivery ownership, though its influence is comparable. If you're looking to run a large organisation, we have other roles for that.

  

What You Can Expect From Us

* The chance to shape the core money platform of Asia Pacific's leading multi\-currency wallet, used by millions of people and businesses.
* Some of the most interesting payments challenges in the region, across multiple markets, currencies, partners and regulators.
* A company that is committed to getting the architecture right, not just shipping fast.
* A culture that values technical craft, direct feedback and getting things done.

**Responsibilities \& Requirements**
  

**1\. Enterprise Database Architecture \& Technical Strategy**
  

Architect, design, and deliver end\-to\-end database solutions across relational (Oracle, PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server) and NoSQL/Distributed databases (MongoDB, Cassandra, Redis).
  

Define enterprise standards for data modeling, partitioning, indexing strategies, and database scalability across high\-volume transactional (OLTP) and analytical (OLAP) environments.
  

Drive the technical roadmap aligned with Citi's enterprise reference architectures, zero\-trust infrastructure, and microservices ecosystem.
  

**2\. Modernization, DBaaS \& Cloud Enablement**

Champion database containerization and modern provisioning frameworks, automating lifecycle management and cluster autoscaling.
  

Partner with application development and cloud architecture teams to re\-platform and refactor applications for cloud\-native persistence layers.
  

**3\. High Availability, Replication \& Scalability Engineering**
  

Architect, configure, and maintain robust High Availability (HA) topologies (e.g., Oracle Data Guard/Active Data Guard, Oracle RAC, PostgreSQL Streaming Replication / Patroni, MongoDB Replica Sets \& Sharded Clusters).
  

Establish cross\-region and multi\-data\-center replication strategies to support 24/7/365 mission\-critical banking operations with minimal RTO (Recovery Time Objective) and zero RPO (Recovery Point Objective).
  

**4\. Advanced Performance Engineering, Tuning \& Diagnostics**
  

Spearhead deep\-dive performance troubleshooting, query optimization, indexing reviews, execution plan analysis, and database profiling across production systems.
  

Establish automated monitoring, telemetry, and observability frameworks (using Prometheus, Grafana, OEM, AppDynamics, and APM tools) to proactively detect anomalies, locking/blocking, and resource bottlenecks.

**5\. Security, Vulnerability Management \& Access Control**
  

Enforce end\-to\-end database security standards, including Transparent Data Encryption (TDE), data masking, tokenization, TLS encryption in\-transit, and privileged access controls.
  

Drive automated security patching, configuration baseline compliance (CIS Benchmarks), and rapid remediation of vulnerabilities (CVEs), ensuring zero non\-compliant instances across the fleet.
  

Integrate identity and credential workflows with enterprise secrets management tools (e.g., HashiCorp Vault, CyberArk) and role\-based access control (RBAC).
  

**6\. Database DevOps, Infrastructure as Code (IaC) \& CI/CD**
  

Champion Database DevOps practices by integrating schema migrations and database deployments into automated CI/CD pipelines (via Harness, Tekton, Jenkins, Bitbucket/GitHub).
  

Develop and maintain Infrastructure as Code (IaC) playbooks and configuration scripts using Ansible, Terraform, and Python/Bash automation.
  

Eliminate manual operational touchpoints through self\-service database provisioning and automated routine maintenance.
  

**7\. Continuity of Business (COB) \& Disaster Recovery (DR)**
  

Own the disaster recovery framework for core database estates, designing and executing regular formal COB/DR failover drills.
  

Define and maintain backup and restore strategies (RMAN, storage snapshots, point\-in\-time recovery) to safeguard data integrity against hardware failures, corruption, and site\-level disasters.
  

Ensure comprehensive auditability and validation of backup retention policies aligned with financial regulatory standards.
  

**8\. Governance, Risk, Audit \& Regulatory Compliance**
  

Serve as the primary database technical authority during internal and external audit reviews, regulatory examinations, and risk assessments.
  

Ensure full compliance with Citi's Information Security policies, data sovereignty regulations (e.g., GDPR, local residency laws), and financial record retention mandates.
  

Maintain comprehensive technical documentation, architecture runbooks, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and operational readiness checklists.
  

**9\. Technical Leadership, Mentorship \& Vendor Engagement**
  

Provide strong technical leadership, guidance, and mentorship to senior engineers, database administrators, and offshore support teams.
  

Collaborate closely with application squads, enterprise architects, site reliability engineers (SREs), and product owners to translate complex business requirements into robust database architectures.
  

Liaise with major database software vendors (Oracle, EnterpriseDB, MongoDB, AWS) on product escalations, feature enhancements, and roadmaps.
  

**10\. Required Qualifications, Experience \& Certifications**  

**Education**: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).
  

**Experience**: 12\+ years of progressive experience in database engineering/administration, with at least 3\+ years in a lead or architect capacity within a large\-scale, enterprise financial services environment.
  

**Core Technical Competencies:**
  

In\-depth expertise in Oracle (19c/21c, RAC, Data Guard) and/or PostgreSQL (v12\+, Patroni, Connection Pooling).
  

Strong working proficiency with NoSQL platforms (MongoDB, Redis) and DBaaS architectures.
  

Demonstrated hands\-on scripting and automation skills in Python, Bash, Ansible, or Terraform.
  

Solid understanding of Linux kernel OS tuning, storage architectures (SAN/NAS/NVMe), and networking protocols.
  

Certifications (Preferred):
  

Certified Oracle Database Administrator / Specialist
  

AWS Certified Database – Specialty or AWS Solutions Architect Professional
  

PostgreSQL / EDB Certified Professional
  

MongoDB Certified DBA Associate / Professional
  

Key Leadership \& Soft Skills
  

Proven track record of managing high\-impact technical incidents and driving root cause analysis (RCA) to conclusion.
  

Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with the ability to articulate complex technical topics to non\-technical stakeholders and executive leadership.
  

Strong ownership mindset, problem\-solving agility, and passion for continuous technology modernization.

The Data Technical Architect is the design authority for the data architecture that underpins the Command Centre and enables the Control Tower. The role owns how operational data from source systems across product domains is ingested, integrated, resolved, modelled, certified, and served as a single, trusted, near real‑time view of the business.
  

This is a data‑architecture‑led role. The primary deliverable is the target‑state data architecture – layering, canonical models, event and entity design, the semantic and KPI layer, and the data quality and lineage framework – that allows the Control Tower to detect exceptions, trigger alerts, and support root‑cause analysis with confidence in the underlying data.

The role works closely with Command Centre operations, BI delivery, Data Engineering, GDA, Data Platform, source system owners, and Enterprise Architecture, and operates within the standards set by the Tech Governance Lead.
 

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES


Data Architecture \& Design


Own the end‑to‑end data architecture for the Command Centre – how data flows from operational source systems across product domains (e.g. Contracts, Ocean) through to the Control Tower consumption layer.


Define the target‑state data architecture and transition roadmap, including the layering model (landing, raw, integrated/curated, consumption) and the storage, compute, and serving choices at each layer.


Design the canonical, cross‑domain data layer that gives the Control Tower one consistent representation of the core business objects, independent of the source systems they originate from.


Define master and reference data requirements, entity resolution, and cross‑system key mapping so that events from different systems resolve to the same business entity.


Establish data domain boundaries, data ownership, and data product definitions aligned to the Command Centre operating model.


Produce and maintain core architecture artefacts – conceptual, logical, and physical data models, data flow and lineage diagrams, integration maps, and architecture decision records.


Data Integration \& Pipeline Architecture


Architect real‑time, near real‑time, and batch ingestion patterns – streaming, event‑driven, CDC, API, and scheduled – and define which pattern applies to which source and use case.


Define the operational event model and payload standards for the milestones, status changes, and exceptions that drive Control Tower views.


Design pipeline patterns for reliability at scale: idempotency, replay, late‑arriving and out‑of‑order events, backfill, and reconciliation back to source.


Set standards for orchestration, dependency management, error and dead‑letter handling, and pipeline observability.


Define and agree data contracts and SLAs with source system teams, covering schema, frequency, volume, and change management.


Define latency, freshness, and throughput targets per data domain and ensure the architecture demonstrably meets them.


Data Modelling \& Semantic / KPI Layer


Design the dimensional, event, and state models required for end‑to‑end milestone tracking, cycle time, dwell, and exception analysis.


Architect the semantic and KPI layer so that each metric is defined once, certified, and reused consistently across Control Tower views and downstream reporting.


Model for drill‑down, so an alert on the Control Tower can be traced to transaction‑level detail and root cause without leaving the platform.


Define the historisation approach – slowly changing dimensions, snapshots, and point‑in‑time reporting – to support trend and retrospective analysis.


Design aggregation, pre‑computation, and caching strategies so Control Tower dashboards meet response‑time expectations at production data volumes.


Data Quality, Governance \& Security


Define data quality dimensions, rules, and thresholds at each architectural layer, and design how failures are detected, quarantined, and escalated.


Ensure Control Tower alerting is built on trusted data – design the freshness, completeness, and validity checks that gate what is surfaced to operations.


Design end‑to‑end metadata and lineage capture, from source system field through to published KPI.


Design role‑based access, row and column level security, masking, retention, and audit into the data architecture rather than bolting it on later.


Ensure alignment with enterprise data architecture, cloud strategy, and BI governance standards, and work with the Tech Governance Lead on dataset certification.


Identify, document, and drive remediation of data architecture technical debt.


Delivery \& Execution


Translate the architecture into sprint‑ready designs, data contracts, and backlog items for data engineering and BI delivery teams.


Provide hands‑on technical direction – prototypes, proofs of concept, performance tuning, and resolution of complex modelling and pipeline problems.


Review data models, pipelines, and semantic layers for adherence to the agreed architecture.


Own volumetrics and capacity planning, and support performance, resilience, and reconciliation testing ahead of each Control Tower release.


Drive reuse of data products, models, and patterns across Command Centre use cases to reduce duplication and rework.


Stakeholder \& Cross\-functional Collaboration


Partner with Command Centre operations and business owners to translate operational visibility and exception‑management needs into concrete data requirements.
